name: Ki No Bi Kyoto Dry Gin
official_name: KI NO BI Kyoto Dry Gin
owner: The Kyoto Distillery (founded by Noriko Kakuda Croll, David Croll, Marcin Miller)
production: 11 botanicals split into six Elements (Base, Citrus, Tea, Herbal, Spice, Fruity & Floral)
Each Element macerated in rice spirit and distilled separately, then blended
Christian Carl hybrid copper stills (140 L and 450 L at launch)
history: 2016 | Distillery opens; Ki No Bi launches in Japan in October 2016
finish: Slightly warming and spicy from ginger root
expressions: Ki No Tea Kyoto Dry Gin | tea-focused, with Hori-Shichimeien gyokuro and tencha
Ki No Bi Sei | navy strength (Skurnik listing title)
Ki No Bi Go | aged gin (Skurnik listing title)
serve_official: Martini with yuzu twist, a grind of sansho pepper or a shiso leaf; ideal mixer classic tonic
notes: Described as Japan's first dedicated/purpose-built gin distillery. Head distiller at launch Alex Davies. Label made with KIRA Karacho, a Kyoto karakami atelier dating to 1624. Only 10 of 11 botanicals named across sources.
